overview: In 2016, I became a Professor Emeritus of Microbiology with four decades of experience as a B cell biologist and molecular immunologist.  I obtained my PhD and completed my first postdoctoral studies at UAB with Drs. Sandy Lawton, John Kearney and Max Cooper, working on B cell development.  I then pursued further post-doctoral training with Dr. Matthias Wabl at the Max Planck Institute, Tübingen, Germany, elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying immunoglobulin heavy chain class switching and allelic exclusion in preB cells.  I was recruited back to UAB in 1983 and rose through the ranks to full professor, continuing to work on mechanisms of early and late B cell development in humans and mice. Although emeritus, I continue to be active in research, teaching and departmental/university functions. I am also a consultant for a biotech firm, Trianni/AbCellera, and for a research institute in Yokohama Japan, The RIKEN Center for Integrative Medical Sciences.
